speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've been having episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; to understand what's happening, please tell me your age and how long these episodes typically last. Also, do you recall anything that triggers them, such as flashing lights or specific sounds?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Childhood Absence Epilepsy with atypical semiology (automatisms/post-ictal confusion suggest complex partial seizures, possibly focal impaired awareness seizures evolving into absence-like presentation).

REQUEST IMAGES: EEG.
